sample_unit: user inputs (mental health crisis test examples)

links.outcome: Appropriateness of LLM responses to suicidal ideation, self-harm, and violence crisis inputs (5-point Likert)
links.effect: Some models (gpt-5-nano, deepseek-v3.2-exp) had very low harmful response rates; others (gpt-4o-mini, Llama-4-Scout, grok-4-fast) had markedly higher unsafe output rates, especially in self-harm and suicidal ideation categories.
links.quote: A nonnegligible proportion of responses was rated as inappropriate or harmful, particularly in the self-harm and suicidal ideation categories.

links.outcome: Recognition of indirect or ambiguous crisis signals by LLMs
links.effect: All models showed systemic weaknesses including poor handling of indirect or ambiguous risk signals, formulaic responses, and frequent misalignment with user context.
links.quote: All models exhibited systemic weaknesses, including poor handling of indirect or ambiguous risk signals, reliance on formulaic responses, and frequent misalignment with user context.

unlisted_practices: Unified clinically informed taxonomy of mental health crisis categories for evaluation
LLM-as-a-judge validated against human experts for crisis response grading

screen.reason: The study develops a benchmark dataset and taxonomy to evaluate and audit multiple LLMs on their safety and crisis-handling capabilities when responding to acute mental health crisis inputs, but does not test an organizational deployment practice or safeguard.
